Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Aerospace Dynamics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, the Q&A session will follow the standard operator instructions. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Global Aerospace Dynamics' Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are John Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Financial Officer; and Tom Keller, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-K and 10-Q, for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those statements.

John Harlan:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Global Aerospace Dynamics delivered a solid performance in Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across commercial aviation, defense aeronautics, missiles, space, and sustainment services. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering long-term value to our shareholders. Today, we'll cover key areas including our expansion of service offerings and customer base, the drivers behind our strong aftermarket performance such as fleet utilization and maintenance cycles, a detailed analysis of our revenue drivers and headwinds, and our free cash flow generation and utilization.

We are particularly excited about the recent advancements in our AeroSustain Digital Suite program and its potential to drive significant recurring revenue growth through predictive maintenance and digital twins. We are seeing strong demand for our defense systems, including F-35 support and hypersonics, and our commercial aerospace business is recovering steadily with narrowbody ramps and widebody aftermarket tailwinds. With that, I'll turn it over to Maria to dive deeper into these operational and financial highlights.

Maria Gonzalez:
Thank you, John, and good morning, everyone. As we unpack our Q3 results, one of our most exciting growth drivers is the strategic expansion of our service offerings and customer base. This represents a deliberate shift toward high-margin, recurring revenue streams that are transforming our business model in the Aerospace & Defense sector. In an industry with long 10-15 year development cycles for new platforms and lumpy upfront costs, we're capitalizing on the sustainment phase, where global defense budgets increasingly emphasize lifecycle support over initial acquisitions.

The numbers underscore this momentum. Services revenue, which includes MRO, logistics sustainment, digital engineering, and advanced analytics, surged 28% year-over-year to $1.2 billion in Q3, now comprising 32% of our total segment revenue, up from 22% last year. This growth is backed by our $18.5 billion services backlog, which grew 35% sequentially, with 65% linked to multi-year IDIQ contracts averaging 5-7 years. Margins are attractive, with services EBITDA at 22.4% this quarter—450 basis points higher than our traditional manufacturing mix—due to scale efficiencies and predictive analytics that cut unplanned downtime by up to 40% for customers.

We've expanded our portfolio well beyond airframe and engine overhauls. Our AeroSustain Digital Suite, integrating AI-driven predictive maintenance with digital twins on Siemens NX and our proprietary PHM algorithms, has secured a $450 million, 5-year task order under the U.S. Navy's Next Generation Logistics Carrier program, similar to Boeing's KC-46 tanker sustainment wins. We're extending this to hypersonic systems, developing vibration monitoring and thermal barrier coating refurbishment for platforms like Lockheed's ARRW. Pilots with a classified DoD customer show 25% faster turnaround and 15% cost savings on test article reworks, setting up follow-on Foreign Military Sales opportunities.

We've also tapped into counter-UAS and collaborative combat aircraft areas. Our SwarmGuard Services division handles depot-level integration and software assurance for loitering munitions and loyal wingman drones, leveraging our C4ISR expertise. This quarter, we signed a $220 million contract with the U.S. Air Force's ABMS family of systems, growing our role in JADC2. In space, orbital debris mitigation and satellite bus reconfiguration services ramped up with a $150 million deal from a commercial NewSpace operator like Rocket Lab, accessing the $10 billion-plus annual in-orbit servicing market projected by McKinsey.

Customer base diversification is key. The U.S. DoD anchors us at 62% of services bookings, but international growth jumped 42% year-over-year to $520 million. In the Indo-Pacific, we've gained preferred provider status for F-35 sustainment with allies like those akin to Japan or Australia, including a $300 million, 10-year ALIS modernization package. In the Middle East, Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 localization efforts yielded a $180 million MRO hub contract for Typhoon and F-15 platforms, surpassing BAE Systems regionally. NATO wins include a €250 million framework with Poland for Black Hawk and Apache support, building on our MH-60 legacy. Commercially, we've captured 15% share in A350 engine bay inspections partnering with GE Aviation, with bookings up 55% amid Airbus delays. Customer concentration from the top five clients fell to 18% from 28% two years ago, supported by 120 new task orders from 45 entities.

This aligns with macro trends: global defense spending reached $2.2 trillion per SIPRI, with sustainment at 40-50% of budgets amid aging inventories, Ukraine, and Taiwan tensions. We're investing $280 million YTD in TRL 8-9 tech like quantum-secured comms for sixth-gen fighters, plus tuck-in M&A such as our $425 million buy of a European UAV sustainment firm for EMEA growth. We guide services to 25-30% growth in FY24, with backlog conversion supporting $2.8-3.2 billion in free cash flow, making us the essential lifecycle partner in persistent conflict and great power competition.

Shifting to aftermarket performance, which remains the crown jewel of our portfolio, delivering high-margin recurring revenues that bolster profitability. In Q3, aftermarket sales hit $2.8 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 5% sequentially, at 42% of total segment revenue. Adjusted operating margins expanded 220 basis points to 31.2%, from demand levers, efficiencies, and services focus.

Fleet utilization drives this, especially in commercial aviation's rebound. Global narrowbody rates are at 82% of pre-COVID per IATA, with our ADX-400 regional jets and Boeing 737 MAX/Airbus A320neo partnerships averaging 11.2 flight hours daily, up from 9.8. Commercial engine aftermarket for PW1500G and ADX-700 saw 22% higher shop visits, with equivalent flight hours up 16% to 1.2 billion; widebody CFM56/V2500 hit 10.5 hours on transatlantic/Asia-Pacific routes.

Defense optempo supports too: U.S. DoD F-35 at 72% sortie rates, up from 65%, boosted ADX-90 power package repairs 25%, with $1.2 billion in 5-year contracts post-Lot 15 ramp. NATO allies like UK/Australia push higher amid tensions, lifting defense aftermarket 14%. North America is 55% of mix with LCC expansion (Southwest/Delta); APAC 28%, up 24% with IndiGo/AirAsia X at 12+ hours; Middle East at 90%+ for Emirates A380/777; Europe at 78% post-Airbus strike.

Maintenance cycles benefit from aging fleets (12+ years average per Cirium), compressing C/D-checks on 777/A330s. We handled 1,450 heavy visits, turn-times at 28 days (15% below benchmarks) via modular kits. ADX-700 TBO now 25,000 hours with CMCs/blade coatings, cutting costs 12%, raising lifecycle revenue per engine to $45 million from $38 million. Defense: Black Hawk UH-60 depot cycles shortened to 240 days via analytics, up rotor/transmission 30%.

AeroDigital on 65% of base uses EHM/digital twins for 95% failure prediction, preempting 22% more visits, $250 million invested for 3x ROI via fewer NFFs/optimized spares. TruePower with Pratt & Whitney mirrors GE's TrueChoice, 85% LTA take rates at 28-32% margins. Supply chain: 40% localized forgings (U.S./India), lead times to 45 days, OEM ASPs up 8%.

We're gaining share with FlexCare outcome contracts for F-35 like Lockheed's ODIN, pay-per-flight-hour, 12 new LTAs $4.5 billion backlog including Qatar A350 gear. Outpacing Boeing's 12% growth with our 18% via 70% digital penetration vs. 50% industry. Raytheon/Northrop strong in missiles, but our aero-defense attach rate 15% higher.

Risks include $100/bbl fuel or recessions curbing 5.5% 2025 ASK growth (ICAO), defense sequestration despite $895 billion FY25 NDAA. Q4 growth 16-18%, FY margins 30.5%; FY26 $12-13 billion, 85% commercial/75% defense utilization, $1 billion digital bookings. Aftermarket to 45%+ mix by 2027, ROIC >25%.

Now, turning to our overall revenue drivers and headwinds. Q3 revenue reached $8.7 billion, up 14% year-over-year—our eighth straight double-digit quarter—with YTD at $17.2 billion above guidance midpoint, from Commercial Aviation and Defense & Space tailwinds.

Defense & Space (52%, $4.5 billion, +18%) led: F-35 $1.2 billion in wings/avionics, Lot 16 $2.8 billion awards; $28 billion F-35 backlog, 1.4x book-to-bill. Hypersonics $450 million ARRW boosters (+25%); space $950 million (+22%) Vulcan/Starshield. U.S. DoD 68%, international $1.1 billion F-35/NATO (UK Tempest $750 million), APAC F-X.

Commercial Aviation (42%, $3.65 billion, +9%): narrowbody $1.8 billion 737/A320 at 52/45/month; MRO $850 million (+32%) at 105% 2019 utilization (IATA); 787 wings $650 million at 5/month.

Services/digital 15% ($1.3 billion, +28%): PHM/digital twins lift F-35 availability 82%, $400 million PBL; 3D-printed F-35 mounts cut times 40%/costs 25%, $200 million spares. $145 billion backlog (+12%), 4.2 years visibility, 65% funded, 1.3x book-to-bill; NGAD IRAD, $1.2 billion DARPA CRADA.

Headwinds: supply chain -150 bps margins, titanium +35% (Russia sanctions, 20% BOM); P&W GTF issues delayed $250 million nacelles, $100 million YTD deferral (dual-source Safran). Labor inflation 6.2% (Oklahoma/Alabama), Boeing quality $80 million rework. China C919 -2-3% APAC share (U.S. ITC moat); 777X slips defer $300 million. Europe +15% defense offsets U.S. CR delays ($500 million); FAA SFMR $150 million capex.

Mitigations: $500 million Resilient Supply Chain 2.0 (India/Mexico offshoring, 20% inventory cut YE24). FY24 organic 10-12%, Defense 1.5x book-to-bill (NGAD/CCA); commercial $4 billion FY25 ramps. Raising FY24 revenue to $35.5-36.5 billion, 12-13% margins.

Finally, free cash flow generation and utilization highlight our strength. Q3 FCF $625 million, YTD $1.2 billion (+25%), on track for $2.3-2.6 billion FY despite headwinds. Operating cash $850 million (+18%) from $145 billion backlog (F-35 Lot 15/NGAD); Defense 65% at 110% EBITDA conversion, DSO 52 (progress payments), inventory 145 days.

Commercial $180 million (787/MRO +15%); Missiles/Space $210 million (LRHW/MDA). CapEx $225 million (3.2% sales): 40% F-35 digital (20% O&S cut), 30% Huntsville AM for rockets, rest space clean-rooms.

Utilization: $850 million YTD—35% ($300 million) debt reduction to 2.1x EBITDA (A- S&P); 25% dividends ($0.28/share, 47th increase, 1.8% yield); $250 million repurchases (1.2% shares, $185 avg, +3% EPS); 40% ($300 million) growth (UK UAV $150 million AUKUS, DEW R&D).

U.S. DoD 55% (FY24 NDAA $886 billion F-35/Block V); international 35% (Saudi Patriot, P-8 Australia/India, Eurofighter). Cash Flow Excellence: $500 million (vendor inventory DPO 95, ERP $400 million unlock), 1.15x book-to-bill, 4.5 years visibility (70% fixed). FY26 FCF margins 12-14%, 8-10% growth (hypersonics/CCA/commercial), $5 billion cash/$2 billion revolver.

John Harlan:
Thank you, Maria. We reported revenue of $8.7 billion, a 14% increase year-over-year. Earnings per share were $2.15. We maintain a strong balance sheet with $5.2 billion in cash and equivalents. Full-year guidance is unchanged at $35.5-36.5 billion revenue. We're managing costs tightly while investing in growth, and committed to shareholder returns via dividends and $3 billion repurchases.

Specific highlights: gross margin at 24.5%, operating income $1.8 billion, free cash flow $625 million.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Josh Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Josh Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the expansion of service offerings, particularly international traction?

John Harlan:
Certainly, Josh. As Maria detailed, international services grew 42% to $520 million, with key wins like F-35 ALIS for Indo-Pacific allies, Saudi MRO hub, and Poland's NATO framework. This diversification reduces risk and taps $2.2 trillion global spend, positioning us for 25-30% FY24 services growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Hi, thanks. I'm curious about aftermarket drivers—any risks to utilization if fuel prices spike?

Maria Gonzalez:
Lisa, fleet utilization is robust at 82-90% across regions, but yes, $100/bbl fuel or recessions could pressure 5.5% 2025 ASK growth. We're insulated by defense optempo (F-35 72%) and digital tools preempting 22% of visits, guiding Q4 16-18% growth and 30.5% margins.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel:
Regarding revenue headwinds, how are you addressing supply chain titanium issues?

John Harlan:
Mike, titanium up 35% hit margins 150 bps, but Resilient Supply Chain 2.0 localizes 40% via U.S./India, dual-sources nacelles, and targets 20% inventory reduction. Our $145 billion backlog and 1.3x book-to-bill keep us on track for 10-12% organic growth.

John Harlan:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation in hypersonics, digital sustainment, and next-gen platforms.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our Q3 2024 earnings call. A replay and transcript will be available on our investor relations website.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
